Deliverable 3, preliminary · Heatwaves, ozone and mortality in Santiago, 2009-2020

Author

Amaru Agüero Jiménez

Published

November 23, 2026

Preliminary

These results use working definitions that the principal investigator has not confirmed: heatwave hw_p95_2d, high ozone o3_idw_gt_p75 (the delivered 24-hour mean, whose limits are shown on the ozone validation page). They show that the pipeline runs from the death records to the interaction measures and how much the answer depends on the definitions. They are not findings to cite.

1 Models

For each death the day of death is compared with the control days of the same municipality, year, month and day of the week, by conditional logistic regression, at single-day lags 0 to 3:

Model Linear predictor Reads as
Heatwave alone β₁ HW Odds ratio of death on a heatwave day
Ozone alone β₂ O3high Odds ratio of death on a high-ozone day
Joint β₁ HW + β₂ O3high Each exposure adjusted for the other
Compound categories β₁₀ E10 + β₀₁ E01 + β₁₁ E11 Heatwave only, high ozone only and both, against neither

Additive interaction comes from the compound model: REOI = OR₁₁ − OR₁₀ − OR₀₁ + 1, AP = REOI / OR₁₁ and S = (OR₁₁ − 1) / [(OR₁₀ − 1) + (OR₀₁ − 1)], with delta-method intervals. The multiplicative ratio OR₁₁ / (OR₁₀ × OR₀₁) is reported next to them.

Code/30_models_main.R 
# 30_models_main.R
# Conditional logistic regression of the case-crossover dataset: single
# exposures, joint model, four-category compound exposure and additive
# interaction (REOI, AP, S).
#
# Inputs
#   Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv    (script 21)
#   Data/Derived/exposure_lagged.csv   (script 21)
# Outputs
#   Output/Tables/models_main_or.csv             odds ratios, headline definition
#   Output/Tables/models_main_interaction.csv    REOI, AP, S, headline definition
#   Output/Tables/models_grid.csv                compound model over the definition grid
#   Output/Tables/models_ozone_continuous.csv    ozone per 10 ppb
#
# Models, for each outcome, subgroup and single-day lag (0 to 3):
#   heatwave   logit P = b1 HW
#   ozone      logit P = b2 O3high
#   joint      logit P = b1 HW + b2 O3high
#   compound   logit P = b10 E10 + b01 E01 + b11 E11        (reference E00)
# The compound model is the joint model with its interaction term written as
# categories: OR11 / (OR10 x OR01) is the multiplicative interaction.
#
# The fits use one row per municipality, day of death and referent day,
# weighted by the number of deaths; tests/test_methods.R shows this equals the
# fit on the individual records.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))

conf_level <- get_param("models", "conf_level")
lags <- unlist(get_param("design", "lags_days"))
heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
ozone_main <- paste0(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_series_main"), "_",
                     get_param("air_pollution", "interpolation_method_main"))
ozone_flag_main <- paste0(ozone_main, "_gt_p", get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main"))
outcomes <- names(get_param("mortality", "cause_groups"))
age_labels <- unlist(get_param("mortality", "age_labels"))

cc <- fread(derived_path("case_crossover.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
cc[, `:=`(date = as.Date(date), case_date = as.Date(case_date))]
lagged <- fread(derived_path("exposure_lagged.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
lagged[, date := as.Date(date)]
stopifnot(all(c(paste0(heatwave_main, "_lag", lags), paste0(ozone_flag_main, "_lag", lags))
              %in% names(lagged)))

# Rows of the case-crossover dataset for an outcome and a subgroup
select_rows <- function(outcome, subgroup) {
  rows <- cc[[outcome]] == TRUE
  if (subgroup %in% age_labels) rows <- rows & cc$age_group == subgroup
  if (subgroup %in% c("male", "female")) rows <- rows & cc$sex == subgroup
  stopifnot(subgroup %in% c("all", age_labels, "male", "female"))
  rows & !is.na(rows)
}

# Collapsed dataset with the position of each row in the lagged exposures
prepare <- function(outcome, subgroup) {
  collapsed <- collapse_case_crossover(cc[select_rows(outcome, subgroup)])
  collapsed[, exposure_row := lagged[collapsed, on = .(com, date), which = TRUE]]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(collapsed$exposure_row))
  collapsed
}

# Attach one heatwave definition and one ozone flag at a lag; keep the strata
# where both are known on every referent day
with_exposure <- function(collapsed, heatwave, ozone_flag, lag) {
  d <- copy(collapsed)
  d[, hw := lagged[[paste0(heatwave, "_lag", lag)]][exposure_row]]
  d[, oz := lagged[[paste0(ozone_flag, "_lag", lag)]][exposure_row]]
  complete <- d[, .(ok = !anyNA(hw) && !anyNA(oz)), by = stratum][ok == TRUE, stratum]
  d <- d[stratum %in% complete]
  d[, `:=`(e10 = as.integer(hw == 1 & oz == 0), e01 = as.integer(hw == 0 & oz == 1),
           e11 = as.integer(hw == 1 & oz == 1))]
  d
}

# Deaths by exposure category on the day of death (lagged as requested)
category_deaths <- function(d) {
  d[case == 1, .(deaths = sum(n_deaths), deaths_e00 = sum(n_deaths[hw == 0 & oz == 0]),
                 deaths_e10 = sum(n_deaths[e10 == 1]), deaths_e01 = sum(n_deaths[e01 == 1]),
                 deaths_e11 = sum(n_deaths[e11 == 1]))]
}

compound_results <- function(d) {
  fit <- fit_conditional_logit(d, c("e10", "e01", "e11"))
  or <- odds_ratios(fit, conf_level)
  interaction <- additive_interaction(coef(fit), vcov(fit), conf_level)
  # Multiplicative interaction: OR11 / (OR10 x OR01), on the log scale
  g <- c(-1, -1, 1)
  log_ratio <- sum(g * coef(fit))
  se_ratio <- sqrt(drop(t(g) %*% vcov(fit) %*% g))
  z <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - conf_level) / 2)
  interaction <- rbind(interaction, data.table(
    measure = "multiplicative ratio", estimate = exp(log_ratio),
    low = exp(log_ratio - z * se_ratio), high = exp(log_ratio + z * se_ratio), null_value = 1
  ))
  list(or = or, interaction = interaction)
}

# ---- 1. Headline definition: all outcomes, subgroups and lags ----------------

subgroups <- c("all", age_labels, "male", "female")
main_jobs <- CJ(outcome = outcomes, subgroup = subgroups, sorted = FALSE)

run_main <- function(i) {
  outcome <- main_jobs$outcome[i]
  subgroup <- main_jobs$subgroup[i]
  collapsed <- prepare(outcome, subgroup)
  or_list <- list()
  interaction_list <- list()
  for (lag in lags) {
    d <- with_exposure(collapsed, heatwave_main, ozone_flag_main, lag)
    counts <- category_deaths(d)
    label <- data.table(outcome = outcome, subgroup = subgroup, lag = lag)
    # A category with no deaths on the day of death has no estimable odds ratio
    estimable <- all(unlist(counts[, .(deaths_e10, deaths_e01, deaths_e11)]) > 0)
    logged <- with_warnings(list(
      single = rbind(
        cbind(model = "heatwave", odds_ratios(fit_conditional_logit(d, "hw"), conf_level)),
        cbind(model = "ozone", odds_ratios(fit_conditional_logit(d, "oz"), conf_level)),
        cbind(model = "joint", odds_ratios(fit_conditional_logit(d, c("hw", "oz")), conf_level))
      ),
      compound = if (estimable) compound_results(d)
    ))
    fit_warnings <- paste(unique(logged$warnings), collapse = " | ")
    or_rows <- logged$value$single
    if (estimable) {
      or_rows <- rbind(or_rows, cbind(model = "compound", logged$value$compound$or))
      interaction_list[[length(interaction_list) + 1]] <- cbind(
        label, logged$value$compound$interaction, counts, fit_warnings = fit_warnings
      )
    }
    or_list[[length(or_list) + 1]] <- cbind(label, or_rows, counts, fit_warnings = fit_warnings)
  }
  list(or = rbindlist(or_list), interaction = rbindlist(interaction_list))
}
# The result does not depend on the number of cores.
main_results <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(main_jobs)), run_main,
                                   mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
failed <- vapply(main_results, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
if (any(failed)) stop("Model run failed: ", main_results[[which(failed)[1]]], call. = FALSE)
main_or <- rbindlist(lapply(main_results, `[[`, "or"))
main_interaction <- rbindlist(lapply(main_results, `[[`, "interaction"))
main_or[, `:=`(heatwave = heatwave_main, ozone = ozone_flag_main)]
main_interaction[, `:=`(heatwave = heatwave_main, ozone = ozone_flag_main)]
fwrite(main_or, file.path(dir_tables, "models_main_or.csv"))
fwrite(main_interaction, file.path(dir_tables, "models_main_interaction.csv"))

# ---- 2. Definition grid: compound model, two outcomes, all lags --------------

heatwaves <- unique(sub("_lag[0-9]+$", "", grep("^hw_", names(lagged), value = TRUE)))
ozone_flags <- unique(sub("_lag[0-9]+$", "", grep("_gt_p[0-9]+_lag", names(lagged), value = TRUE)))
grid_outcomes <- c("non_accidental", "cardiopulmonary")
grid_jobs <- CJ(outcome = grid_outcomes, heatwave = heatwaves, ozone = ozone_flags, sorted = FALSE)
grid_data <- lapply(setNames(grid_outcomes, grid_outcomes), prepare, subgroup = "all")

run_grid <- function(i) {
  job <- grid_jobs[i]
  rbindlist(lapply(lags, function(lag) {
    d <- with_exposure(grid_data[[job$outcome]], job$heatwave, job$ozone, lag)
    counts <- category_deaths(d)
    # A category with no deaths on the day of death has no estimable odds ratio
    if (any(unlist(counts[, .(deaths_e10, deaths_e01, deaths_e11)]) == 0)) {
      return(cbind(job, lag = lag, counts, estimable = FALSE))
    }
    logged <- with_warnings(compound_results(d))
    compound <- logged$value
    or <- dcast(compound$or[, .(term, or, or_low, or_high)], . ~ term,
                value.var = c("or", "or_low", "or_high"))[, !"."]
    measures <- dcast(compound$interaction[, .(measure = gsub(" ", "_", tolower(measure)),
                                               estimate, low, high)],
                      . ~ measure, value.var = c("estimate", "low", "high"))[, !"."]
    cbind(job, lag = lag, counts, estimable = TRUE, or, measures,
          fit_warnings = paste(unique(logged$warnings), collapse = " | "))
  }), fill = TRUE)
}
grid_results <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(grid_jobs)), run_grid,
                                   mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
failed <- vapply(grid_results, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
if (any(failed)) stop("Grid run failed: ", grid_results[[which(failed)[1]]], call. = FALSE)
fwrite(rbindlist(grid_results, fill = TRUE), file.path(dir_tables, "models_grid.csv"))

# ---- 3. Ozone as a continuous exposure, per 10 ppb ---------------------------

ozone_series <- as.vector(outer(c("o3", "o3obs", "o3mda8"), c("idw", "ok"), paste, sep = "_"))
continuous <- rbindlist(lapply(grid_outcomes, function(outcome) {
  collapsed <- grid_data[[outcome]]
  rbindlist(lapply(ozone_series, function(series) rbindlist(lapply(lags, function(lag) {
    d <- copy(collapsed)
    d[, ozone_10ppb := lagged[[paste0(series, "_lag", lag)]][exposure_row] / 10]
    d[, hw := lagged[[paste0(heatwave_main, "_lag", lag)]][exposure_row]]
    complete <- d[, .(ok = !anyNA(ozone_10ppb) && !anyNA(hw)), by = stratum][ok == TRUE, stratum]
    d <- d[stratum %in% complete]
    rbind(
      cbind(outcome = outcome, series = series, lag = lag, adjustment = "none",
            odds_ratios(fit_conditional_logit(d, "ozone_10ppb"), conf_level)),
      cbind(outcome = outcome, series = series, lag = lag, adjustment = heatwave_main,
            odds_ratios(fit_conditional_logit(d, c("ozone_10ppb", "hw")), conf_level))
    )[term == "ozone_10ppb"]
  }))))
}))
fwrite(continuous, file.path(dir_tables, "models_ozone_continuous.csv"))

message("Models written: ", nrow(main_or), " odds ratios (headline), ",
        nrow(grid_jobs) * length(lags), " grid fits")

h0 <- headline[lag == 0 & model == "compound"]
r_main <- main_int[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" & measure == "REOI"]

With the working definitions, on the day of exposure the odds of non-accidental death are 1.07 (1.03 to 1.10) times higher on heatwave-only days, 1.03 (1.02 to 1.05) on high-ozone-only days and 1.10 (1.06 to 1.13) on days with both, each against days with neither. The associations weaken with the lag. The joint odds ratio is close to what the two single excesses add up to: the REOI interval includes zero at every lag (lag 0: -0.004 (-0.052 to 0.045); lag 1: 0.008 (-0.040 to 0.056); lag 2: 0.021 (-0.026 to 0.068); lag 3: 0.029 (-0.017 to 0.076)).

5 Across the grid of definitions

The compound model was fitted for every combination of the 15 heatwave definitions, the three ozone series, the two interpolation methods and the three cut-offs, at each lag. The figure shows the REOI for non-accidental mortality with the IDW series; a dot marks the cells whose 95% interval excludes zero. The colour scale stops at ±0.15: the few cells beyond it, all in the rarest heatwave definitions, are drawn at the limit.

Show the code

                     labels = c("Delivered 24 h", "Rebuilt 24 h", "Rebuilt MDA8"))]
g[, cutoff := paste0("> P", sub(".*_gt_p", "", ozone))]

  geom_point(data = g[excludes_zero == TRUE], size = 1.2, colour = ink$primary) +

With 2132 cells and no correction for multiple comparisons, about 107 intervals would exclude zero by chance alone. The full grid is in Output/Tables/models_grid.csv.

5.1 Where the positive cells are

Show the code 
by_threshold <- grid[estimable == TRUE & outcome == "non_accidental", .(
  cells = .N, above_zero_pct = 100 * mean(low_reoi > 0), median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi)
), by = .(threshold = sub("^hw_(.*)_[0-9]d$", "\\1", heatwave), lag)]
by_threshold[, threshold := factor(threshold, levels = c("p90", "p95", "p99", "30c", "ehf"),
                                   labels = c("> P90", "> P95", "> P99", "> 30 °C", "EHF > 0"))]
kable(dcast(by_threshold, threshold ~ lag, value.var = c("above_zero_pct", "median_reoi")),
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
      col.names = c("Heatwave threshold", paste("% above zero, lag", 0:3), paste("Median REOI, lag", 0:3)))

At lags 0 and 1 the grid shows no additive interaction under any definition. At lags 2 and 3 many intervals lie above zero, and they are concentrated in the definitions with the fixed 30 °C threshold and the excess heat factor, while the 95th and 99th percentile definitions show almost none. This is not yet evidence of synergy. Each model looks at one lag at a time, so the exposure of two or three days earlier is not separated from the heat of the days that followed, and days with both exposures belong to longer and hotter spells than heatwave-only days. Models with the lags fitted together (distributed lag models) and with temperature intensity in the model are needed before this pattern is interpreted.

  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.35) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_series) +
  labs(x = "Lag (days)", y = "Odds ratio per 10 ppb", colour = NULL)
Show the code 
cont_table <- copy(continuous)[, value := ci(or, or_low, or_high, 3)]
cont_table[, outcome := cause_labels[outcome]]
kableExtra::scroll_box(
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    kable(dcast(cont_table, outcome + series + adjustment ~ lag, value.var = "value"), format = "html",
          col.names = c("Outcome", "Ozone series", "Adjusted for", "Lag 0", "Lag 1", "Lag 2", "Lag 3")),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
  height = "380px"
)

A 10 ppb step is not the same contrast in the three series: the MDA8 is about twice the 24-hour mean and varies about twice as much from day to day.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 2) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
# Very wide confidence limits are written as long integers; read them as numbers
as_numeric_columns <- function(dt, pattern) {
  columns <- grep(pattern, names(dt), value = TRUE)
  dt[, (columns) := lapply(.SD, as.numeric), .SDcols = columns]
  dt[]
}
# The synergy index has no useful interval when the sum of the two single
# excesses is close to zero
ci_measure <- function(measure, estimate, low, high, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(measure == "S" & (is.na(low) | high / low > 1e3),
         paste(fmt(estimate, digits), "(interval not informative)"),
         ci(estimate, low, high, digits))
}
main_or <- read_table("models_main_or.csv")
main_int <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("models_main_interaction.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high)$")
grid <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("models_grid.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high|or)_")
continuous <- read_table("models_ozone_continuous.csv")

heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
ozone_flag_main <- unique(main_or$ozone)
cause_labels <- c(
  non_accidental = "Non-accidental", cardiopulmonary = "Cardiopulmonary",
  cardiovascular = "Cardiovascular", ischemic_heart = "Ischemic heart disease",
  acute_myocardial_infarction = "Acute myocardial infarction",
  hypertensive = "Hypertensive diseases", cerebrovascular = "Cerebrovascular",
  ischemic_stroke = "Ischemic stroke", hemorrhagic_stroke = "Hemorrhagic stroke",
  respiratory = "Respiratory", copd = "COPD"
)
term_labels <- c(hw = "Heatwave", oz = "High ozone", e10 = "Heatwave only (E10)",
                 e01 = "High ozone only (E01)", e11 = "Heatwave and high ozone (E11)")
model_labels <- c(heatwave = "Heatwave alone", ozone = "Ozone alone", joint = "Joint",
                  compound = "Compound categories")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Preliminary

These results use working definitions that the principal investigator has not
confirmed: heatwave `r heatwave_main`, high ozone `r ozone_flag_main` (the
delivered 24-hour mean, whose limits are shown on the
[ozone validation page](03_ozone_validation.html)). They show that the pipeline
runs from the death records to the interaction measures and how much the
answer depends on the definitions. They are not findings to cite.
:::

## Models

For each death the day of death is compared with the control days of the same
municipality, year, month and day of the week, by conditional logistic
regression, at single-day lags 0 to 3:

| Model | Linear predictor | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| Heatwave alone | β₁ HW | Odds ratio of death on a heatwave day |
| Ozone alone | β₂ O3high | Odds ratio of death on a high-ozone day |
| Joint | β₁ HW + β₂ O3high | Each exposure adjusted for the other |
| Compound categories | β₁₀ E10 + β₀₁ E01 + β₁₁ E11 | Heatwave only, high ozone only and both, against neither |

Additive interaction comes from the compound model:
REOI = OR₁₁ − OR₁₀ − OR₀₁ + 1, AP = REOI / OR₁₁ and
S = (OR₁₁ − 1) / [(OR₁₀ − 1) + (OR₀₁ − 1)], with delta-method intervals.
The multiplicative ratio OR₁₁ / (OR₁₀ × OR₀₁) is reported next to them.


## Non-accidental mortality, working definitions

```{r}
kable(counts, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Lag", "Deaths", "Neither (E00)", "Heatwave only (E10)",
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.6

compound[, category := factor(c(e10 = "Heatwave only", e01 = "High ozone only",
                                e11 = "Heatwave and high ozone")[term],
                              levels = c("High ozone only", "Heatwave only", "Heatwave and high ozone"))]
ggplot(compound, aes(factor(lag), or, colour = category)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.35) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_compound[levels(compound$category)]) +
```

```{r}
#| label: headline-text
h0 <- headline[lag == 0 & model == "compound"]
r_main <- main_int[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" & measure == "REOI"]
```

With the working definitions, on the day of exposure the odds of non-accidental
death are `r ci(h0[term == "e10", or], h0[term == "e10", or_low], h0[term == "e10", or_high])`
times higher on heatwave-only days, `r ci(h0[term == "e01", or], h0[term == "e01", or_low], h0[term == "e01", or_high])`
on high-ozone-only days and `r ci(h0[term == "e11", or], h0[term == "e11", or_low], h0[term == "e11", or_high])`
on days with both, each against days with neither. The associations weaken
with the lag. The joint odds ratio is close to what the two single excesses
add up to: the REOI interval includes zero at every lag
(`r paste(sprintf("lag %d: %s", r_main$lag, ci(r_main$estimate, r_main$low, r_main$high, 3)), collapse = "; ")`).

### Additive interaction


## By age and sex

```{r}
#| label: fig-subgroups
#| fig-cap: "Non-accidental mortality by age group and sex: odds ratio of days with both exposures (E11) and REOI, by lag. Bars are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-height: 4.6
sub_or <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup != "all" & model == "compound" & term == "e11",
                  .(subgroup, lag, measure = "Odds ratio, E11", estimate = or,
                    low = or_low, high = or_high, null = 1)]

subgroups <- rbind(sub_or, sub_reoi)
subgroups[, subgroup := factor(subgroup, levels = c("0-64", "65-84", "85+", "female", "male"),
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-subgroup-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Difference between subgroups in the log odds ratio of the compound exposure (E11): two-sample z-test against the first subgroup of each pair."
e11 <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & model == "compound" & term == "e11" & subgroup != "all",
               .(subgroup, lag, log_or, se)]
pairs <- list(c("0-64", "65-84"), c("0-64", "85+"), c("female", "male"))
tests <- rbindlist(lapply(pairs, function(pair) {
  d <- merge(e11[subgroup == pair[1]], e11[subgroup == pair[2]], by = "lag", suffixes = c("_a", "_b"))
  d[, .(comparison = paste(pair[2], "against", pair[1]), lag,
        ratio_of_odds_ratios = exp(log_or_b - log_or_a),
        z = (log_or_b - log_or_a) / sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2))][
    , p_value := 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))]
}))
kable(tests, digits = c(0, 0, 3, 2, 3),
      col.names = c("Comparison", "Lag", "Ratio of odds ratios", "z", "p"))
```

## Across the grid of definitions

The compound model was fitted for every combination of the 15 heatwave
definitions, the three ozone series, the two interpolation methods and the
three cut-offs, at each lag. The figure shows the REOI for non-accidental
mortality with the IDW series; a dot marks the cells whose 95% interval
excludes zero. The colour scale stops at ±0.15: the few cells beyond it, all
in the rarest heatwave definitions, are drawn at the limit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "REOI for non-accidental mortality across heatwave definitions (rows) and ozone definitions (columns), by lag, IDW series."
#| fig-height: 13
#| fig-width: 9
g <- grid[outcome == "non_accidental" & grepl("_idw_", ozone) & estimable == TRUE]
g[, series := factor(sub("_idw_gt_p[0-9]+$", "", ozone), levels = c("o3", "o3obs", "o3mda8"),
                     labels = c("Delivered 24 h", "Rebuilt 24 h", "Rebuilt MDA8"))]
g[, cutoff := paste0("> P", sub(".*_gt_p", "", ozone))]
g[, heatwave := factor(heatwave, levels = rev(unique(grid$heatwave)))]
g[, excludes_zero := low_reoi > 0 | high_reoi < 0]
limit <- 0.15
ggplot(g, aes(cutoff, heatwave, fill = estimate_reoi)) +
  geom_tile(colour = ink$surface, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = g[excludes_zero == TRUE], size = 1.2, colour = ink$primary) +
  facet_grid(paste("Lag", lag) ~ series) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = diverging[["low"]], mid = diverging[["mid"]], high = diverging[["high"]],
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-limit, limit), oob = scales::squish, name = "REOI") +
  labs(x = "Ozone cut-off (municipality percentile)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "center")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Definition grid, summary by outcome and lag: number of fitted cells, range of the REOI and cells whose 95% interval excludes zero."
grid_summary <- grid[estimable == TRUE, .(
  cells = .N, median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi), min_reoi = min(estimate_reoi),
  max_reoi = max(estimate_reoi), above_zero = sum(low_reoi > 0), below_zero = sum(high_reoi < 0)
), keyby = .(outcome, lag)]
grid_summary[, outcome := cause_labels[outcome]]
kable(grid_summary, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Outcome", "Lag", "Cells", "Median REOI", "Lowest REOI", "Highest REOI",
                    "Interval above zero", "Interval below zero"))
```

With `r grid[estimable == TRUE, .N]` cells and no correction for multiple
comparisons, about `r round(0.05 * grid[estimable == TRUE, .N])` intervals would
exclude zero by chance alone. The full grid is in `Output/Tables/models_grid.csv`.

### Where the positive cells are

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid-threshold
#| tbl-cap: "Non-accidental mortality: share of grid cells (%) whose REOI interval lies above zero, by heatwave threshold and lag, with the median REOI."
by_threshold <- grid[estimable == TRUE & outcome == "non_accidental", .(
  cells = .N, above_zero_pct = 100 * mean(low_reoi > 0), median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi)
), by = .(threshold = sub("^hw_(.*)_[0-9]d$", "\\1", heatwave), lag)]
by_threshold[, threshold := factor(threshold, levels = c("p90", "p95", "p99", "30c", "ehf"),
                                   labels = c("> P90", "> P95", "> P99", "> 30 °C", "EHF > 0"))]
kable(dcast(by_threshold, threshold ~ lag, value.var = c("above_zero_pct", "median_reoi")),
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
      col.names = c("Heatwave threshold", paste("% above zero, lag", 0:3), paste("Median REOI, lag", 0:3)))
```

At lags 0 and 1 the grid shows no additive interaction under any definition.
At lags 2 and 3 many intervals lie above zero, and they are concentrated in
the definitions with the fixed 30 °C threshold and the excess heat factor,
while the 95th and 99th percentile definitions show almost none. This is not
yet evidence of synergy. Each model looks at one lag at a time, so the
exposure of two or three days earlier is not separated from the heat of the
days that followed, and days with both exposures belong to longer and hotter
spells than heatwave-only days. Models with the lags fitted together
(distributed lag models) and with temperature intensity in the model are
needed before this pattern is interpreted.

```{r}
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
```

```{r}
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
```

A 10 ppb step is not the same contrast in the three series: the MDA8 is about
twice the 24-hour mean and varies about twice as much from day to day.
